nodes.title: A stock page shows adjusted price, daily return and volume over time, with splits, dividends, membership periods and delisting marked.

criteria: Given a stock with a split, when its page opens, then the split is marked on the chart on its date.

nodes.title: The researcher can browse validation results for any snapshot.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when its validation view opens, then every quarantined or flagged record is listed with its check and reason, filterable by check and by stock.

nodes.title: The researcher can see data coverage across the universe over time.

criteria: Given the coverage view, when it opens, then it shows member count and missing-bar count for every trading date in coverage.

nodes.title: Charts and layouts are built with the dataviz and frontend-design skills.

criteria: Given any chart or page in the app, when reviewed, then it follows those skills' guidance; a chart passes only if it is legible in both light and dark themes.

nodes.title: A running download or validation shows live progress.

criteria: Given a run in progress, when the monitor is open, then completed and total counts update within 2 seconds of each change.

nodes.title: Failures appear while the run is going.

criteria: Given a stock that fails during a run, when the monitor is open, then the failure and its reason appear within 2 seconds.

nodes.title: Past runs are listed with their records.

criteria: Given completed runs, when the run list opens, then each shows type, start and end time, outcome, and counts, and opens to its full record (INGST-06).

nodes.title: Opening the monitor partway through a run shows the run's state so far.

criteria: Given a run already 40% done, when the monitor is opened, then it shows current progress and all failures so far, not only events after opening.

nodes.title: One schedule defines the test periods for every method.

criteria: Given any two methods scored by the platform, when their results are compared, then they cover exactly the same test periods.

nodes.title: Test periods are consecutive blocks of 21 trading days, and the first starts after at least 756 trading days of history.

criteria: Given the covered history, when the schedule is built, then test blocks are 21 trading days, non-overlapping, consecutive, and the first begins on or after trading day 757.

nodes.title: A gap separates each training window from its test period: at least 5 trading days, and never shorter than the longest label horizon the method uses.

criteria: Given a method whose labels look 21 days ahead, when its training data for a test period starting on day T is assembled, then no label's horizon ends on or after T, and the last training date is at least 21 trading days before T.

nodes.title: A method sees only data available by the end of its training window when it is fitted.

criteria: Given a fit for a test period, when any input dated after the training window's end reaches the fit, then the run fails with a look-ahead error.

nodes.title: The most recent 504 trading days are a held-back lockbox, scored once per hypothesis only after its walk-forward result is recorded.

criteria: Given a hypothesis with no recorded walk-forward outcome, when lockbox scoring is requested, then it is refused.
Given a hypothesis already scored on the lockbox, when lockbox scoring is requested again, then it is refused.

nodes.title: The universe in every test period is the membership as of its start.

criteria: Given a test period starting on T, when portfolios are formed, then only stocks that were members on T are eligible.

nodes.title: A hypothesis is registered with its claim, null, metric, test, significance level, correction family, snapshot and test periods before it runs.

criteria: Given a hypothesis missing any of these fields, when registration is attempted, then it is refused with the missing fields named.

nodes.title: A registered hypothesis cannot be edited once its run starts.

criteria: Given a hypothesis whose run has started, when an edit is attempted, then it is refused; the researcher can only register a new, linked hypothesis.

nodes.title: Every test is run with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the registered metric and test periods.

criteria: Given a registered hypothesis, when it is tested, then the skill receives the registered null, metric, periods and correction family; the hypothesis passes only if the null is rejected at 5% after multiple-testing correction across its family.

nodes.title: Every outcome is recorded, failures included.

criteria: Given a completed test, when the ledger is read, then the entry shows the statistic, corrected p-value, effect size, and pass or fail.

nodes.title: No comparison, ranking or claim is reported without a registered ledger entry.

criteria: Given a comparison run with no registered hypothesis, when its result is requested, then it is refused.

nodes.title: The ledger can be listed by stage, feature and outcome.

criteria: Given the ledger, when filtered to failed S3 hypotheses, then exactly those entries are listed.

nodes.title: Portfolios rebalance at the start of each test period and drift with returns within it.

criteria: Given weights set at the start of a 21-day block, when the block is simulated, then daily weights drift with each stock's returns until the next rebalance.

nodes.title: Trading costs of 10 basis points per side are charged on traded value.

criteria: Given a rebalance trading 20% of portfolio value, when costs are applied, then 0.02% of portfolio value is deducted.

nodes.title: Each test period reports realised variance, after-cost return, turnover, and Sharpe ratio net of the risk-free rate.

criteria: Given a completed backtest, when its results are read, then all four values are present for every test period.

nodes.title: A held stock that is delisted is closed at its delisting return.

criteria: Given a position in a stock delisted mid-period, when simulated, then the delisting return is applied and the proceeds are held as cash until the next rebalance.

nodes.title: Factors are estimated only on each training window, never the full sample.

criteria: Given a test period starting on T, when its residual returns are computed, then factor loadings come from a fit whose data ends before T.

nodes.title: The number of factors is chosen per window: those whose eigenvalues exceed what pure-noise returns of the same shape would produce.

criteria: Given a window of pure-noise returns, when factors are chosen, then 0 are kept in at least 95% of 100 simulated trials.

nodes.title: Residual returns show much less cross-correlation than raw returns.

criteria: Given any training window, when residuals are computed, then the mean absolute pairwise correlation of residuals is at most 50% of that of raw returns, checked with the data-analysis skill.

nodes.title: Stocks are included only for the dates they have data; nothing is zero-filled.

criteria: Given a stock that joined mid-window, when factors are fitted, then its missing dates are excluded, not filled.

nodes.title: Residual returns are available as of any date for later stages.

criteria: Given a date T, when residual returns up to T are requested, then they use only loadings fitted before T.

nodes.title: Noise eigenvalues are replaced and signal eigenvalues are kept.

criteria: Given a window's correlation matrix, when denoised, then eigenvalues above the pure-noise edge are unchanged and those below it are replaced by their average.

nodes.title: The denoised matrix is a valid correlation matrix.

criteria: Given any denoised matrix, when checked, then it is symmetric, positive definite, and has a unit diagonal within 1e-10.

nodes.title: Denoising is fitted only on the training window.

criteria: Given a test period starting on T, when its denoised matrix is built, then it uses only returns dated before the window's end.

nodes.title: Each estimator is scored by the realised out-of-sample variance of the minimum-variance portfolio built from it.

criteria: Given an estimator, when scored, then the score is the realised variance over all walk-forward test periods of its long-only minimum-variance portfolio from BTEST.

nodes.title: Estimators are characterised with the data-analysis skill before ranking.

criteria: Given the estimators on the training windows, when characterised, then the skill reports eigenvalue spectra, condition numbers and stability across windows for each estimator.

nodes.title: Each estimator's improvement over the sample estimate is a registered hypothesis tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given an estimator, when compared with the sample estimate, then the skill tests the paired per-period variance differences; the estimator ranks above the sample estimate only if its lower variance is significant at 5% after correction across all estimator comparisons.

nodes.title: The ranking is published with every estimator's score, effect size and ledger outcome.

criteria: Given the completed comparison, when the ranking is read, then every estimator appears, failures included.

nodes.title: Each portfolio is long-only and fully invested, with no stock above 5% weight.

criteria: Given any portfolio's weights at a rebalance, when checked, then all are ≥ 0, sum to 1 within 1e-9, and none exceeds 0.05.

nodes.title: Minimum variance, risk parity and hierarchical risk parity are each built from the top-ranked COV estimator.

criteria: Given the COV ranking, when portfolios are built, then all three use the estimator ranked first.

nodes.title: Each risk-based portfolio's lower variance versus equal weight is a registered hypothesis tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given a portfolio, when compared with equal weight, then the skill tests paired per-period realised variances; it passes only if significant at 5% after correction across the three comparisons.

nodes.title: The ranking reports realised variance, after-cost return, Sharpe ratio and turnover for all four portfolios.

criteria: Given the completed comparison, when read, then all four portfolios appear with all four metrics and their ledger outcomes.

nodes.title: The minimum-variance portfolio's after-cost results are stored as the benchmark for S4.

criteria: Given S4 comparisons, when they run, then they use these stored per-period results on the same test periods.

nodes.title: Risk parity gives each stock equal risk contribution under the estimated covariance.

criteria: Given a risk-parity portfolio at a rebalance, when risk contributions are computed with the estimator used to build it, then each is within 1% (relative) of the average.

nodes.title: A feature value on date T uses only data known by T's close.

criteria: Given any feature, when its value for T is recomputed with all data after T removed, then it is unchanged.

nodes.title: Features are computed for every member on every date where their lookback has enough data, and are missing elsewhere.

criteria: Given a stock with 30 days of history and a 63-day feature, when computed, then the value is missing, not zero or partial.

nodes.title: At least 10 candidate features are defined before S3 testing starts, each with a written rationale.

criteria: Given the start of S3 testing, when the feature list is read, then at least 10 features are listed, each with its lookback and rationale.

nodes.title: Each feature's distribution and stability are characterised with the data-analysis skill before testing.

criteria: Given a feature, when characterised, then the skill reports coverage, distribution and tails, and correlation with the other candidates across time windows.

nodes.title: Each feature is tested against the next 5-day residual return from FACT.

criteria: Given a feature on date T, when its information is measured, then the target is the residual return from T+1 through T+5, with residuals fitted before T.

nodes.title: Each feature's information gain is a registered hypothesis tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the walk-forward test periods.

criteria: Given a feature, when tested, then the skill tests the mean per-period cross-sectional rank correlation with the target against zero; the feature passes only if it is significant at 5% after correction across every S3 feature tested.

nodes.title: The surviving features are recorded as the only engineered inputs S4 may use.

criteria: Given S4 training, when a feature not in the surviving list is supplied, then it is refused.

nodes.title: Every feature's outcome is recorded, failures included.

criteria: Given S3 is complete, when the ledger is filtered to S3, then every candidate in FEAT appears with its outcome.

nodes.title: Forecast targets are forward log return and forward realised volatility over 1, 5 and 21 trading days, counted in trading days, not rows.

criteria: Given a stock with a halt day inside the horizon, when its 5-day target is built, then the horizon spans 5 exchange trading days and the target is missing if any day lacks a bar.

nodes.title: Training windows respect the walk-forward gap for the longest target horizon.

criteria: Given a forecaster trained for a test period starting on T, when its training samples are assembled, then no sample's target ends on or after T (WFWD-03).

nodes.title: Inputs known in advance, observed inputs and fixed attributes are kept separate, and fixed attributes are point-in-time.

criteria: Given a stock whose sector changed, when samples before the change are built, then they carry the earlier sector.

nodes.title: Normalisation statistics come only from each training window.

criteria: Given a test sample, when it is normalised, then the statistics used were computed on that period's training window only.

nodes.title: The volatility forecaster must beat trailing 63-day realised volatility and an exponentially weighted volatility baseline.

criteria: Given forecasts on all test periods, when compared with each baseline by the null-hypothesis-testing skill on per-period mean log-volatility squared error, then the forecaster passes only if better than both at 5% after correction.

nodes.title: The return forecaster must beat a zero-return forecast.

criteria: Given forecasts on all test periods, when tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on mean per-period cross-sectional rank correlation with realised returns, then it passes only if above zero at 5% after correction; its rank correlation must also exceed the best single surviving S3 feature's.

nodes.title: Every training run is reproducible from its recorded snapshot, settings and seed.

criteria: Given a recorded run, when it is re-run on the same hardware, then test-period forecasts match within 1e-6.

nodes.title: A volatility-forecast portfolio is judged on realised variance against the S2 minimum-variance portfolio.

criteria: Given its per-period results, when compared by the null-hypothesis-testing skill with PORT-05's stored results, then it passes only if its realised variance is lower at 5% after correction across all FPORT and AGENT comparisons.

nodes.title: A return-forecast portfolio is judged on after-cost Sharpe ratio against the S2 minimum-variance portfolio.

criteria: Given its per-period after-cost results, when compared by the null-hypothesis-testing skill with PORT-05's stored results, then it passes only if its Sharpe ratio is higher at 5% after correction across all FPORT and AGENT comparisons.

nodes.title: Forecast-driven portfolios meet the same constraints as classical ones.

criteria: Given any FPORT weights, when checked, then they satisfy PORT-01.

nodes.title: Agents train only in simulations built from training-window data.

criteria: Given an agent trained for a test period starting on T, when its training episodes are inspected, then none contains data dated on or after the training window's end.

nodes.title: Each agent line registers a budget of at most 20 configurations before training starts.

criteria: Given an agent line with 20 configurations tried, when a 21st is attempted, then it is refused.

nodes.title: An agent is judged on after-cost Sharpe ratio against the S2 minimum-variance portfolio.

criteria: Given its per-period after-cost results, when compared by the null-hypothesis-testing skill with PORT-05's stored results, then it passes only if its Sharpe ratio is higher at 5% after correction across all FPORT and AGENT comparisons, including every configuration tried.

nodes.title: An agent line whose budget is used up with no pass stops, and is recorded as failed.

criteria: Given a line with every configuration failed, when another training run is requested for it, then it is refused and the ledger shows the line as stopped.
Given any agent action, when applied, then the weights satisfy PORT-01.

nodes.title: The verdict lists every S4 method with its walk-forward outcome, lockbox outcome and effect size versus the benchmark.

criteria: Given S4 is complete, when the verdict is produced, then every FPORT and AGENT ledger entry appears, failures included.

nodes.title: A method is declared to beat the classical portfolios only if it passed walk-forward and was not significantly worse on the lockbox.

criteria: Given a method that passed walk-forward but whose lockbox Sharpe ratio is lower than the benchmark's at 5% significance, when the verdict is written, then the method is not declared a winner.

nodes.title: The verdict states one conclusion: which methods beat the benchmark, or that none does.

criteria: Given the verdict, when read, then its first line names the winning methods or says "none".

nodes.title: Daily S&P 500 membership history with effective dates for every addition and removal, covering at least 15 years.

criteria: Given the dataset, when the earliest date with complete membership is read, then it is at least 15 years before the latest date.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume for every stock ever a member, from 252 trading days before its first membership through its last trading day, delisted stocks included.

criteria: Given any stock ever a member, when its history is checked, then bars exist from 252 trading days before it joined (or its listing, if later) through its delisting or the present.

nodes.title: Corporate actions for every such stock: splits, cash dividends, spin-offs, ticker changes and delistings, each with its date, and for delistings the reason and final price or payout where one exists.

criteria: Given a stock known to have split, when its corporate actions are read, then the split appears with its ratio and effective date.

nodes.title: Every record carries the date it became known, as well as the date it refers to.

criteria: Given any stored record, when read, then both dates are present.

nodes.title: The US equity exchange trading calendar for the covered history.

criteria: Given any date in coverage, when queried, then the calendar says whether US exchanges traded that day.

nodes.title: A daily short-term risk-free interest rate for the covered history.

criteria: Given any trading date in coverage, when queried, then a rate is returned.

nodes.title: A sector classification for every stock, with the dates each classification applied.

criteria: Given a stock reclassified in year Y, when its sector is read for a date before Y, then the earlier sector is returned.

nodes.title: Data costs beyond the existing price subscription are at most $50 a month.

criteria: Checked by listing every paid data source and its monthly price in the architecture.

nodes.title: Rented GPU spending is at most $100 a month.

criteria: Checked against the monthly rental invoices.

nodes.title: All analysis except neural-network training runs on one laptop: a daily update download plus validation finishes in at most 15 minutes, and a full history rebuild in at most 6 hours.

criteria: Timed on the laptop and recorded in the run records.

nodes.title: The browser app is reachable only from the local machine.

criteria: Checked by connecting from another device on the same network: the connection is refused.

nodes.title: Downloaded vendor data never leaves the laptop, apart from training copies sent to rented GPU machines, which are deleted when the rental ends.

criteria: Checked by reviewing every outbound data transfer in the architecture and the rental shutdown steps.

nodes.title: Every data shape exchanged between the analysis side and the browser app is declared once, and both sides are checked against it.

criteria: Checked by changing a field on one side only: the build check fails.

nodes.title: Every reported result can be reproduced from its recorded snapshot, settings and seed.

criteria: Checked by re-running a sample of 3 ledger entries per stage: CPU results match within 1e-9 (GPU results per FCST-07).

nodes.title: The explorer shows a single stock's full history within 2 seconds and a membership date within 1 second.

criteria: Timed in the browser on the laptop with the full dataset.

Every result rests on daily data I can trust: index membership as of each date, delisted stocks included, corporate actions applied, every download validated.
"Out of sample" means one thing everywhere: every method is scored on the same walk-forward test periods, with a gap so training never sees test outcomes.
No claim without a test: each hypothesis is written down before it is run, tested against chance, and its outcome recorded, failures included.
A method earns its place only by beating a simpler benchmark out of sample. Classical risk-based portfolios are judged on realised variance; anything driven by machine learning must beat them.
I can explore the dataset and watch download and validation runs live in a local browser app.
The system returns the S&P 500 member list as of any trading date in the covered history.

criteria: Given a trading date D in coverage, when membership is requested for D, then every stock whose membership was effective on D is returned and no other stock is.
Given any trading date in coverage, when membership is requested, then the count is between 495 and 510.

nodes.title: Members that were later removed or delisted appear on the dates they were members.

criteria: Given a company that was removed from the index after a bankruptcy, when membership is requested for a date before its removal, then it is included.

nodes.title: Each stock carries a permanent identifier that never changes and is never reused.

criteria: Given a ticker that was used by two different companies at different times, when either company's history is requested, then only that company's data is returned.
Given a company that changed ticker, when its history is requested by its identifier, then it is one unbroken series across the change.

nodes.title: Membership history is reproduced: it agrees with publicly announced index changes.

criteria: Given a check set of at least 30 publicly announced index additions and removals spread across the covered history (at least 5 of them delisted companies), when membership is compared with them, then every change takes effect on the announced effective date.

nodes.title: A full download fetches the complete history for every stock that was ever a member.

criteria: Given an empty store, when a full download completes, then every identifier returned by UNIV-01 for any covered date has price history covering its membership period.

nodes.title: An update download fetches only data newer than the last successful run, plus any vendor revisions.

criteria: Given a store last updated on day D, when an update runs on day D+3, then only records dated after D or revised since D are fetched.

nodes.title: Every download produces an immutable, dated snapshot that later runs never overwrite.

criteria: Given two successful downloads, when either snapshot is requested afterwards, then it returns exactly the data that run stored.

nodes.title: A vendor revision to an already-stored record is kept as a new version with both values on record.

criteria: Given a stored close that the vendor later revises, when the update completes, then both the old and the new value are retrievable, each with the date it was known.

nodes.title: A run that fails partway leaves the last good snapshot untouched and can be resumed.

criteria: Given a download interrupted after half the stocks, when the researcher resumes it, then only the unfinished stocks are fetched and the previous snapshot is still readable throughout.

nodes.title: Every run records its start and end time, scope, record counts, and any errors.

criteria: Given a completed or failed run, when its record is opened, then all of these fields are present.

nodes.title: No snapshot becomes the current dataset until validation passes.

criteria: Given a snapshot with a blocking failure, when validation completes, then the previous current dataset stays current and the run record says why.

nodes.title: Price records are checked for internal consistency.

criteria: Given a daily bar with a non-positive price, high below low, or close outside [low, high], when validated, then it is quarantined with the failed check named.

nodes.title: Every member stock has a bar on every exchange trading day of its membership, or a recorded reason (halt, suspension) for the gap.

criteria: Given a member missing a bar on a trading day with no recorded reason, when validated, then the gap is reported as a failure.

nodes.title: Large daily moves must be explained.

criteria: Given an adjusted daily return beyond ±40%, when validated, then it passes only if a corporate action, a delisting or a recorded researcher override explains it; otherwise it is flagged for review.

Given a stock with a split or dividend on day D, when its adjusted return for D is computed, then it equals the economic total return (price change plus dividend, split-neutral) within 0.01 percentage points.

nodes.title: Membership integrity is checked on every snapshot.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when validated, then a failure is reported for any date whose member count falls outside 495–510 and for any member with no price data on a membership date.

nodes.title: Each promoted snapshot gets a data-quality report produced with the data-analysis skill.

criteria: Given a promoted snapshot, when the report is produced, then it covers coverage by date, missingness, return distributions and tails, and quarantined-record counts by check; it passes only if every quarantined record is listed with its reason.
Given two bars for the same stock and date in one snapshot, when validated, then both are quarantined and the failure is blocking.

nodes.title: An as-of-T request never returns information published after T's close.

criteria: Given a request as of T, when any record is returned, then its known-date is on or before T.
Given a membership change announced before T but effective after T, when membership as of T is requested, then the change is not applied.

nodes.title: A returns panel for a date range contains only stocks that were members on each date.

criteria: Given a returns panel for a range, when a stock joined the index mid-range, then its returns appear only from its effective join date.

nodes.title: A delisted stock's final return, through its last price or delisting payout, is included.

criteria: Given a stock delisted after a cash acquisition, when its returns are requested, then the last return reflects the cash paid per share.

Given a stock delisted after bankruptcy with no final price, when its returns are requested, then the last return is flagged as estimated and a delisting return of −100% is applied unless a final price is recorded.
Given a stock with no bar on a trading day, when returns are requested, then that cell is reported missing, never zero.

nodes.title: Every request can be pinned to a snapshot so results can be reproduced.

criteria: Given a request pinned to snapshot X, when it is repeated after newer snapshots exist, then the output is identical.

nodes.title: Daily risk-free rates are available for the same dates as prices.

criteria: Given any trading date in coverage, when the risk-free rate is requested, then a daily rate is returned.

nodes.title: The researcher can view the member list for any covered date.

criteria: Given a selected date, when the membership view opens, then it lists every member with identifier, ticker on that date, and join date.

nodes.title: The researcher can open any stock ever in the universe, delisted ones included.

criteria: Given a delisted stock, when searched by any ticker it ever used, then its page opens with its full history.

nodes.title: A stock page shows adjusted price, daily return and volume over time, with splits, dividends, membership periods and delisting marked.

criteria: Given a stock with a split, when its page opens, then the split is marked on the chart on its date.

nodes.title: The researcher can browse validation results for any snapshot.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when its validation view opens, then every quarantined or flagged record is listed with its check and reason, filterable by check and by stock.

nodes.title: The researcher can see data coverage across the universe over time.

criteria: Given the coverage view, when it opens, then it shows member count and missing-bar count for every trading date in coverage.

nodes.title: Charts and layouts are built with the dataviz and frontend-design skills.

criteria: Given any chart or page in the app, when reviewed, then it follows those skills' guidance; a chart passes only if it is legible in both light and dark themes.

nodes.title: A running download or validation shows live progress.

criteria: Given a run in progress, when the monitor is open, then completed and total counts update within 2 seconds of each change.

nodes.title: Failures appear while the run is going.

criteria: Given a stock that fails during a run, when the monitor is open, then the failure and its reason appear within 2 seconds.

nodes.title: Past runs are listed with their records.

criteria: Given completed runs, when the run list opens, then each shows type, start and end time, outcome, and counts, and opens to its full record (INGST-06).

nodes.title: Opening the monitor partway through a run shows the run's state so far.

criteria: Given a run already 40% done, when the monitor is opened, then it shows current progress and all failures so far, not only events after opening.

nodes.title: One schedule defines the test periods for every method.

criteria: Given any two methods scored by the platform, when their results are compared, then they cover exactly the same test periods.

nodes.title: Test periods are consecutive blocks of 21 trading days, and the first starts after at least 756 trading days of history.

criteria: Given the covered history, when the schedule is built, then test blocks are 21 trading days, non-overlapping, consecutive, and the first begins on or after trading day 757.

nodes.title: A gap separates each training window from its test period: at least 5 trading days, and never shorter than the longest label horizon the method uses.

criteria: Given a method whose labels look 21 days ahead, when its training data for a test period starting on day T is assembled, then no label's horizon ends on or after T, and the last training date is at least 21 trading days before T.

nodes.title: A method sees only data available by the end of its training window when it is fitted.

criteria: Given a fit for a test period, when any input dated after the training window's end reaches the fit, then the run fails with a look-ahead error.

nodes.title: The most recent 504 trading days are a held-back lockbox, scored once per hypothesis only after its walk-forward result is recorded.

criteria: Given a hypothesis with no recorded walk-forward outcome, when lockbox scoring is requested, then it is refused.
Given a hypothesis already scored on the lockbox, when lockbox scoring is requested again, then it is refused.

nodes.title: The universe in every test period is the membership as of its start.

criteria: Given a test period starting on T, when portfolios are formed, then only stocks that were members on T are eligible.

nodes.title: A hypothesis is registered with its claim, null, metric, test, significance level, correction family, snapshot and test periods before it runs.

criteria: Given a hypothesis missing any of these fields, when registration is attempted, then it is refused with the missing fields named.

nodes.title: A registered hypothesis cannot be edited once its run starts.

criteria: Given a hypothesis whose run has started, when an edit is attempted, then it is refused; the researcher can only register a new, linked hypothesis.

nodes.title: Every test is run with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the registered metric and test periods.

criteria: Given a registered hypothesis, when it is tested, then the skill receives the registered null, metric, periods and correction family; the hypothesis passes only if the null is rejected at 5% after multiple-testing correction across its family.

nodes.title: Every outcome is recorded, failures included.

criteria: Given a completed test, when the ledger is read, then the entry shows the statistic, corrected p-value, effect size, and pass or fail.

nodes.title: No comparison, ranking or claim is reported without a registered ledger entry.

criteria: Given a comparison run with no registered hypothesis, when its result is requested, then it is refused.

nodes.title: The ledger can be listed by stage, feature and outcome.

criteria: Given the ledger, when filtered to failed S3 hypotheses, then exactly those entries are listed.

nodes.title: Portfolios rebalance at the start of each test period and drift with returns within it.

criteria: Given weights set at the start of a 21-day block, when the block is simulated, then daily weights drift with each stock's returns until the next rebalance.

nodes.title: Trading costs of 10 basis points per side are charged on traded value.

criteria: Given a rebalance trading 20% of portfolio value, when costs are applied, then 0.02% of portfolio value is deducted.

nodes.title: Each test period reports realised variance, after-cost return, turnover, and Sharpe ratio net of the risk-free rate.

criteria: Given a completed backtest, when its results are read, then all four values are present for every test period.

nodes.title: A held stock that is delisted is closed at its delisting return.

criteria: Given a position in a stock delisted mid-period, when simulated, then the delisting return is applied and the proceeds are held as cash until the next rebalance.

nodes.title: Factors are estimated only on each training window, never the full sample.

criteria: Given a test period starting on T, when its residual returns are computed, then factor loadings come from a fit whose data ends before T.

nodes.title: The number of factors is chosen per window: those whose eigenvalues exceed what pure-noise returns of the same shape would produce.

criteria: Given a window of pure-noise returns, when factors are chosen, then 0 are kept in at least 95% of 100 simulated trials.

nodes.title: Residual returns show much less cross-correlation than raw returns.

criteria: Given any training window, when residuals are computed, then the mean absolute pairwise correlation of residuals is at most 50% of that of raw returns, checked with the data-analysis skill.

nodes.title: Stocks are included only for the dates they have data; nothing is zero-filled.

criteria: Given a stock that joined mid-window, when factors are fitted, then its missing dates are excluded, not filled.

nodes.title: Residual returns are available as of any date for later stages.

criteria: Given a date T, when residual returns up to T are requested, then they use only loadings fitted before T.

nodes.title: Noise eigenvalues are replaced and signal eigenvalues are kept.

criteria: Given a window's correlation matrix, when denoised, then eigenvalues above the pure-noise edge are unchanged and those below it are replaced by their average.

nodes.title: The denoised matrix is a valid correlation matrix.

criteria: Given any denoised matrix, when checked, then it is symmetric, positive definite, and has a unit diagonal within 1e-10.

nodes.title: Denoising is fitted only on the training window.

criteria: Given a test period starting on T, when its denoised matrix is built, then it uses only returns dated before the window's end.

nodes.title: Each estimator is scored by the realised out-of-sample variance of the minimum-variance portfolio built from it.

criteria: Given an estimator, when scored, then the score is the realised variance over all walk-forward test periods of its long-only minimum-variance portfolio from BTEST.

nodes.title: Estimators are characterised with the data-analysis skill before ranking.

criteria: Given the estimators on the training windows, when characterised, then the skill reports eigenvalue spectra, condition numbers and stability across windows for each estimator.

nodes.title: Each estimator's improvement over the sample estimate is a registered hypothesis tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given an estimator, when compared with the sample estimate, then the skill tests the paired per-period variance differences; the estimator ranks above the sample estimate only if its lower variance is significant at 5% after correction across all estimator comparisons.

nodes.title: The ranking is published with every estimator's score, effect size and ledger outcome.

criteria: Given the completed comparison, when the ranking is read, then every estimator appears, failures included.

nodes.title: Each portfolio is long-only and fully invested, with no stock above 5% weight.

criteria: Given any portfolio's weights at a rebalance, when checked, then all are ≥ 0, sum to 1 within 1e-9, and none exceeds 0.05.

nodes.title: Minimum variance, risk parity and hierarchical risk parity are each built from the top-ranked COV estimator.

criteria: Given the COV ranking, when portfolios are built, then all three use the estimator ranked first.

nodes.title: Each risk-based portfolio's lower variance versus equal weight is a registered hypothesis tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given a portfolio, when compared with equal weight, then the skill tests paired per-period realised variances; it passes only if significant at 5% after correction across the three comparisons.

nodes.title: The ranking reports realised variance, after-cost return, Sharpe ratio and turnover for all four portfolios.

criteria: Given the completed comparison, when read, then all four portfolios appear with all four metrics and their ledger outcomes.

nodes.title: The minimum-variance portfolio's after-cost results are stored as the benchmark for S4.

criteria: Given S4 comparisons, when they run, then they use these stored per-period results on the same test periods.

nodes.title: Risk parity gives each stock equal risk contribution under the estimated covariance.

criteria: Given a risk-parity portfolio at a rebalance, when risk contributions are computed with the estimator used to build it, then each is within 1% (relative) of the average.

nodes.title: A feature value on date T uses only data known by T's close.

criteria: Given any feature, when its value for T is recomputed with all data after T removed, then it is unchanged.

nodes.title: Features are computed for every member on every date where their lookback has enough data, and are missing elsewhere.

criteria: Given a stock with 30 days of history and a 63-day feature, when computed, then the value is missing, not zero or partial.

nodes.title: At least 10 candidate features are defined before S3 testing starts, each with a written rationale.

criteria: Given the start of S3 testing, when the feature list is read, then at least 10 features are listed, each with its lookback and rationale.

nodes.title: Each feature's distribution and stability are characterised with the data-analysis skill before testing.

criteria: Given a feature, when characterised, then the skill reports coverage, distribution and tails, and correlation with the other candidates across time windows.

nodes.title: Each feature is tested against the next 5-day residual return from FACT.

criteria: Given a feature on date T, when its information is measured, then the target is the residual return from T+1 through T+5, with residuals fitted before T.

nodes.title: Each feature's information gain is a registered hypothesis tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the walk-forward test periods.

criteria: Given a feature, when tested, then the skill tests the mean per-period cross-sectional rank correlation with the target against zero; the feature passes only if it is significant at 5% after correction across every S3 feature tested.

nodes.title: The surviving features are recorded as the only engineered inputs S4 may use.

criteria: Given S4 training, when a feature not in the surviving list is supplied, then it is refused.

nodes.title: Every feature's outcome is recorded, failures included.

criteria: Given S3 is complete, when the ledger is filtered to S3, then every candidate in FEAT appears with its outcome.

nodes.title: Forecast targets are forward log return and forward realised volatility over 1, 5 and 21 trading days, counted in trading days, not rows.

criteria: Given a stock with a halt day inside the horizon, when its 5-day target is built, then the horizon spans 5 exchange trading days and the target is missing if any day lacks a bar.

nodes.title: Training windows respect the walk-forward gap for the longest target horizon.

criteria: Given a forecaster trained for a test period starting on T, when its training samples are assembled, then no sample's target ends on or after T (WFWD-03).

nodes.title: Inputs known in advance, observed inputs and fixed attributes are kept separate, and fixed attributes are point-in-time.

criteria: Given a stock whose sector changed, when samples before the change are built, then they carry the earlier sector.

nodes.title: Normalisation statistics come only from each training window.

criteria: Given a test sample, when it is normalised, then the statistics used were computed on that period's training window only.

nodes.title: The volatility forecaster must beat trailing 63-day realised volatility and an exponentially weighted volatility baseline.

criteria: Given forecasts on all test periods, when compared with each baseline by the null-hypothesis-testing skill on per-period mean log-volatility squared error, then the forecaster passes only if better than both at 5% after correction.

nodes.title: The return forecaster must beat a zero-return forecast.

criteria: Given forecasts on all test periods, when tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on mean per-period cross-sectional rank correlation with realised returns, then it passes only if above zero at 5% after correction; its rank correlation must also exceed the best single surviving S3 feature's.

nodes.title: Every training run is reproducible from its recorded snapshot, settings and seed.

criteria: Given a recorded run, when it is re-run on the same hardware, then test-period forecasts match within 1e-6.

nodes.title: A volatility-forecast portfolio is judged on realised variance against the S2 minimum-variance portfolio.

criteria: Given its per-period results, when compared by the null-hypothesis-testing skill with PORT-05's stored results, then it passes only if its realised variance is lower at 5% after correction across all FPORT and AGENT comparisons.

nodes.title: A return-forecast portfolio is judged on after-cost Sharpe ratio against the S2 minimum-variance portfolio.

criteria: Given its per-period after-cost results, when compared by the null-hypothesis-testing skill with PORT-05's stored results, then it passes only if its Sharpe ratio is higher at 5% after correction across all FPORT and AGENT comparisons.

nodes.title: Forecast-driven portfolios meet the same constraints as classical ones.

criteria: Given any FPORT weights, when checked, then they satisfy PORT-01.

nodes.title: Agents train only in simulations built from training-window data.

criteria: Given an agent trained for a test period starting on T, when its training episodes are inspected, then none contains data dated on or after the training window's end.

nodes.title: Each agent line registers a budget of at most 20 configurations before training starts.

criteria: Given an agent line with 20 configurations tried, when a 21st is attempted, then it is refused.

nodes.title: An agent is judged on after-cost Sharpe ratio against the S2 minimum-variance portfolio.

criteria: Given its per-period after-cost results, when compared by the null-hypothesis-testing skill with PORT-05's stored results, then it passes only if its Sharpe ratio is higher at 5% after correction across all FPORT and AGENT comparisons, including every configuration tried.

nodes.title: An agent line whose budget is used up with no pass stops, and is recorded as failed.

criteria: Given a line with every configuration failed, when another training run is requested for it, then it is refused and the ledger shows the line as stopped.
Given any agent action, when applied, then the weights satisfy PORT-01.

nodes.title: The verdict lists every S4 method with its walk-forward outcome, lockbox outcome and effect size versus the benchmark.

criteria: Given S4 is complete, when the verdict is produced, then every FPORT and AGENT ledger entry appears, failures included.

nodes.title: A method is declared to beat the classical portfolios only if it passed walk-forward and was not significantly worse on the lockbox.

criteria: Given a method that passed walk-forward but whose lockbox Sharpe ratio is lower than the benchmark's at 5% significance, when the verdict is written, then the method is not declared a winner.

nodes.title: The verdict states one conclusion: which methods beat the benchmark, or that none does.

criteria: Given the verdict, when read, then its first line names the winning methods or says "none".

nodes.title: Daily S&P 500 membership history with effective dates for every addition and removal, covering at least 15 years.

criteria: Given the dataset, when the earliest date with complete membership is read, then it is at least 15 years before the latest date.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume for every stock ever a member, from 252 trading days before its first membership through its last trading day, delisted stocks included.

criteria: Given any stock ever a member, when its history is checked, then bars exist from 252 trading days before it joined (or its listing, if later) through its delisting or the present.

nodes.title: Corporate actions for every such stock: splits, cash dividends, spin-offs, ticker changes and delistings, each with its date, and for delistings the reason and final price or payout where one exists.

criteria: Given a stock known to have split, when its corporate actions are read, then the split appears with its ratio and effective date.

nodes.title: Every record carries the date it became known, as well as the date it refers to.

criteria: Given any stored record, when read, then both dates are present.

nodes.title: The US equity exchange trading calendar for the covered history.

criteria: Given any date in coverage, when queried, then the calendar says whether US exchanges traded that day.

nodes.title: A daily short-term risk-free interest rate for the covered history.

criteria: Given any trading date in coverage, when queried, then a rate is returned.

nodes.title: A sector classification for every stock, with the dates each classification applied.

criteria: Given a stock reclassified in year Y, when its sector is read for a date before Y, then the earlier sector is returned.

nodes.title: Data costs beyond the existing price subscription are at most $50 a month.

criteria: Checked by listing every paid data source and its monthly price in the architecture.

nodes.title: Rented GPU spending is at most $100 a month.

criteria: Checked against the monthly rental invoices.

nodes.title: All analysis except neural-network training runs on one laptop: a daily update download plus validation finishes in at most 15 minutes, and a full history rebuild in at most 6 hours.

criteria: Timed on the laptop and recorded in the run records.

nodes.title: The browser app is reachable only from the local machine.

criteria: Checked by connecting from another device on the same network: the connection is refused.

nodes.title: Downloaded vendor data never leaves the laptop, apart from training copies sent to rented GPU machines, which are deleted when the rental ends.

criteria: Checked by reviewing every outbound data transfer in the architecture and the rental shutdown steps.

nodes.title: Every data shape exchanged between the analysis side and the browser app is declared once, and both sides are checked against it.

criteria: Checked by changing a field on one side only: the build check fails.

nodes.title: Every reported result can be reproduced from its recorded snapshot, settings and seed.

criteria: Checked by re-running a sample of 3 ledger entries per stage: CPU results match within 1e-9 (GPU results per FCST-07).

nodes.title: The explorer shows a single stock's full history within 2 seconds and a membership date within 1 second.

criteria: Timed in the browser on the laptop with the full dataset.

acceptance: Each type is code in its owner's `types.py` (or `packages/app/src/wire/`, `packages/app/src/types.ts`); each `tests/contracts/<id>.<Type>/` sample validates against its schema; `schema.json` is exported from the bodies and `wire.ts` generated from it

Every M1 step and entry imports with its contract signature, body `NotImplementedError("<its task>")`; each `__init__.py` exports its contract; `qrp_data.__main__` dispatches `download` (then validate on the staged snapshot) and `validate`, `qrp_server.__main__` dispatches `serve` and `export-schema`
The `data.membership_as_of`, `data.returns_panel` and `server.get_membership` fakes serve their fixtures
`open_run` inserts a row in a temp `runs.sqlite` (WAL) and heartbeats every 2 s on an injected clock; `close_run` writes end time, counts, errors and status; both validate as data.RunRecord
A `qrp.toml` naming the synthetic vendor gives a data.Source; a vendor with a missing key raises `CredentialsError` before any fetch

`SyntheticSource(seed=7)` satisfies data.Source: 505 members on every XNYS session 2020-01-02 – 2022-12-30, every plants-s1 event present, each planted removal paired with a same-session addition, `truth` exposed; same seed, same rows
On the data.Source replay double, returns every permaticker ever in SP500, appended as parts; validates as data.StockId
On the data.Source double, SEP and ACTIONS per stock (since the watermark on update) go through `store.append_parts` with known dates stamped, one event per stock; `--resume` skips finished stocks
On the data.Source double, DTB3 is stored in full with carried rates `filled=True`, and the SIC history per CIK is stored as dated intervals

`stage_snapshot` writes a `staged` manifest of the previous snapshot's parts plus this run's and never touches `CURRENT`; `resolve_snapshot` reads it back, `CURRENT` when None, `SnapshotError` when unknown
`exchange_calendars` XNYS sessions clipped to the data.Snapshot sample's coverage; behaves as the data.Calendar double on 2001-09 and 2012-10
high ≥ low, open and close inside [low, high], prices > 0 and volume ≥ 0 on the data.Snapshot sample; each failure a data.Issue

nodes.title: check_gaps spine (bar per member per session)

acceptance: On the data.Snapshot sample and data.Calendar double, a missing bar with no recorded halt and an SEP date XNYS calls closed are each a data.Issue
On the data.ReturnsPanel sample, |return| > 40% with no action, delisting or override is a `flagged` data.Issue
On every action day of the data.Snapshot and data.ReturnsPanel samples, an AD-08 total return more than 0.01 pp from `closeadj`'s is a data.Issue
On the `data.membership_as_of` fake, a session outside 495–510 members is a data.Issue; with no announced-changes set, none is checked
Rows sharing (stock, ref_date, known_date) in the data.Snapshot sample are each a blocking data.Issue
Six data.Issue samples give `issues.parquet`, quarantined records and `blocking` True only when a blocking issue exists; validates as data.ValidationResult
A passing data.ValidationResult builds the sorted read view and renames `CURRENT` atomically; blocking or `promote=False` leaves `CURRENT` alone
The data.QualityInputs sample gives `quality.md` with sections `coverage`, `missingness`, `returns`, `quarantine`; both outputs validate against their contract folders
DuckDB over the data.Snapshot sample's parts: newest version known by `as_of`, AD-08 returns, member mask, NaN gaps, the gap and delisting returns; validates as data.ReturnsPanel
On the data.Snapshot sample, SP500 changes replayed from their effective dates to the session on or before the date; `CoverageError` outside; validates as data.Membership
A loopback host passes; any other raises 403 with `ErrorBody(bad_request)`
On the `data.membership_as_of` fake, returns data.Membership; `CoverageError` → 422 `out_of_coverage`, `SnapshotError` → 409 `no_dataset`
The data.Membership sample maps field for field, dates as ISO strings; validates against tests/contracts/server.MembershipBody/
`model_json_schema` of every body written to a given path; the output validates as server.WireSchema
On the `server.get_membership` fake, the hook returns the server.MembershipBody sample for a date and surfaces `ErrorBody` samples as errors

Renders every server.MembershipBody sample as a date picker, a "resolved to <used>" note and a sortable member table linking to stock pages, and `ErrorBody(no_dataset)` as the no-dataset state linking to `/runs`, in light and dark
On the current server.WireSchema sample, regenerates `wire.ts` and reports `changed` False; validates as app.WireModule
Validates every sample under `tests/contracts/server.*/` except `server.WireSchema/` against the body its folder names; a broken sample is a `failures` entry; validates as app.FixtureReport
